props.heading: Best trips from Atlanta on a budget
props.subheading: Real flight, hotel, and activity costs for the destinations that actually fit what you have to spend — flying out of ATL.

props.text: Delta flies nonstop from Atlanta to both a beach destination (Cancún) and a ski destination (Aspen) — Oaxaca is the one that needs a connection. Flying out of ATL, a trip to Oaxaca can start around $1,130 for flight, hotel, and activities together — not just the flight, pulled from our own cost data, not guesses.

features.title: Cancún — nonstop, ~2h44m
features.text: Delta runs about 43 nonstop flights a week out of its ATL hub.

features.title: Oaxaca — no nonstop from any airline
features.text: Every routing connects — via Cancún, Dallas, Houston, or Mexico City — pushing total travel to 6.5–9+ hours each way.

features.title: Aspen — nonstop, ~4h01m
features.text: Delta flies it nonstop, and recently doubled winter frequency to 2 flights a day — a real, growing route, not a token seasonal add.

props.text: Atlanta's nonstop coverage splits cleanly: easy direct access to a beach trip and a ski trip, but zero nonstop options to Oaxaca on any carrier. Delta's decision to double ATL–Aspen winter frequency to twice daily is a concrete signal of real, growing demand for that route specifically.

items.question: Are these real-time prices?
items.answer: They're estimates based on our own curated cost data for this route and season, not a live quote — the real price on the partner site may be a bit higher or lower depending on exact dates.

items.question: Is Oaxaca doable as a long weekend from Atlanta?
items.answer: It's tight — no nonstop exists on any airline, so realistic door-to-door time is 6.5+ hours each way with a layover, which eats into a short trip fast.

items.question: Is there a direct flight to Aspen from Atlanta?
items.answer: Yes, on Delta — and they recently doubled winter frequency to twice a day, a real sign of growing demand on that specific route.
